confidence_note: Book not read. Old text's fMRI reward-center claim and TOMS Shoes example are unsupported and dropped. Story is built on the 2009 Niemiec, Ryan and Deci graduates study (confirmed in the PMC copy), tied to Pink only through his purpose-versus-profit framing and his use of Deci and Ryan's work. Whether Drive itself cites this exact study is unconfirmed, so the story attributes the study to the Rochester group. Study is correlational and self-reported.
facts: Pink names purpose as the third driver after autonomy and mastery; he frames purpose maximization against profit maximization and puts Deci and Ryan's work at the center.

Niemiec, Ryan and Deci (2009) had recent graduates rate the importance of extrinsic aims (money, fame, image) and intrinsic aims (personal growth, relationships, community) at one and two years after college.
Placing importance on either type predicted attaining it.
Attaining intrinsic aims related to better psychological health; attaining extrinsic aims did not and was linked to indicators of ill-being.
The effect ran through satisfaction of needs for autonomy, competence and relatedness.
Authors suggest striving for wealth and adulation does little to satisfy these needs early in a career and can crowd out more nourishing activities.
Press coverage mentioned shame, anger and physical anxiety symptoms such as headaches.
scene_details: lists of aims: money, fame, image
ratings at one year and two years
headaches and stomachaches in the press summary
tension: People who reached what they chased were not equally better off.
opening_idea: Graduates rating what they care about, twice.

lessons.idea: Check whether a goal feeds your basic needs, not just whether you reach it.

reflect_final: Which goal on your list would still matter to you if nobody ever saw you reach it?

use_cases.situation: You are choosing your next goal
use_cases.move: Ask whom you'd do it with and what you'd learn.

use_cases.situation: A friend weighs a job mostly for pay
use_cases.move: Ask which part would still feel theirs in a year.
Ask which they would do if nobody saw.

pocket_idea: Reaching growth and community goals went with better health; reaching money and fame goals did not.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: In a graduates study, reaching growth goals helped health and reaching money goals did not.
